Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:10:1.english: [They] do not require appraisal - That assessors appraise them before she receives them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:10:2.hebrew: צריכי שומא - וכיון שלא שמאום תחלה, אינה מקודשת, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:10:2.english: [They] require appraisal - And since they did not appraise them beforehand, she is not betrothed, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:10:3.hebrew: בכל דהו - התקדשי לי בהן כמו שהן. דלא צריכי שומא — דבציר מפרוטה לא שוו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:10:3.english: By any amount - “Be betrothed to me with them as they are.” [And the reason] that they do not require an appraisal [is] that they are not worth less than a *peruta*.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:11:1.hebrew: אי דאמר - התקדשי לי בחמשים זוז, והרי לך אלו בדמיהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:11:1.english: If he said - “Be betrothed to me for fifty zuz, and here you have these [garments] for their value.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:11:2.english: And they are worth fifty - However, experts had not appraised it prior to this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:12:1.hebrew: שוה כסף ככסף - גבי קידושין כסף כתיב, ושוה כסף איתרבי ככסף, כדאמרינן לקמן: ״ישיב״ לרבות שוה כסף. הלכך, כי כסף — בעינן דקייץ:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:12:1.english: [An item] worth money [is] like money - Regarding betrothal, money is written [in Scripture], and [an item] worth money was included [by derivation] to be like money, as we say later: “He shall return” [serves] to include [an item] worth money. Therefore, like money, we require that it be fixed [in value].

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:1:1.hebrew: בעלי חיים נדחים - אם נדחו, ידחו לעולם. ואיכא למ"ד (ביומא דף סד.): אין דיחוי אלא בשחוטין, אבל בעלי חיים שנדחו חוזרים ונראין, ולדידיה קריבה הך בהמה כשחזר ולקח חציה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:1:1.english: Living animals can be deferred - If they were deferred, they are deferred forever. And there is an authority who holds (in Yoma 64a) that deferral applies only to slaughtered [animals], but living animals that were deferred become eligible again; and according to him, this animal would be offered when he went back and purchased its [other] half.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:2:1.hebrew: דיחוי מעיקרא - כגון זו, שמתחילת הקדישה לא נראית ליקרב. ואיכא למ"ד (בסוכה דף לג:) דפליג ואמר: אין דיחוי אלא בנראה ונדחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:2:1.english: Deferral at the outset - Such as this [case], where from the beginning of its consecration it was not fit to be sacrificed. And there is an authority (in Sukkah 33b) who disagrees and says: Deferral applies only to [that which was] fit and [subsequently] deferred.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:2:2.hebrew: יש דיחוי בדמים - יש תורת דיחוי בדבר שאינו קדוש אלא לדמיו, כגון זו שמתחלה לא הקדישה אלא לדמיה — שתמכר ויקדשו דמי חציה, שהרי ליקרב לחצאין לא היתה ראויה — ואפ"ה חל עלה תורת דיחוי לדחות מעל המזבח לעולם, ולא אמרינן אין דיחוי אלא בדבר שהוקדש לגופו ליקרב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:2:2.english: There is deferral with regard to monetary value - The principle of deferral applies to an item that is consecrated only for its monetary value, such as this [animal], which from the outset he consecrated only for its value — that it should be sold and the value of its half become consecrated, for it was not fit to be sacrificed in halves — and even so, the principle of deferral took effect upon it to defer it from the altar forever; and we do not say that there is deferral only regarding an item that was consecrated in its body to be sacrificed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:3:1.english: He divided [the betrothal] - And he is [considered] like one who betroths in halves.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:3:2.hebrew: מונה והולך הוא - ורישא דמילתא אמסקנא נמי קאי, ולאו לחצאין הוא, דהא חצי פרוטה לאו בר תפיסה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:3:2.english: He was counting - And the beginning of the statement also relates to the conclusion, and it is not [intended to take effect] in halves, for half a peruta is not capable of taking effect [for betrothal].

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:4:1.hebrew: כיון דאמר בפרוטה פסקה - ולא היה תחילת דבורו אלא לחציה, וטעה לומר שמקדשין לחצאין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:4:1.english: Since he said, "With a peruta," he divided [his statement] - And the beginning of his statement was only for half of her, and he mistakenly thought that one can betroth [a woman] in halves.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:4:2.english: All on that day - Since it is his intention to complete it today.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:7:1.english: To my two sons - And they are adults, and they made him an agent to betroth [for them].

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:8:1.hebrew: או דילמא בתך בפרוטה - דמידע ידע דבבציר מפרוטה לא מקדשה, ופרתו לא אמר על פרוטה, אלא שתקנה לו כשימשכנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:8:1.english: Or perhaps your daughter with a peruta - For he is well aware that with less than a peruta she is not betrothed, and regarding his cow, he did not say [that it be acquired] for the peruta, but rather that it should be acquired by him when he pulls it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 7b:9:1.english: Your land through taking possession - When I take possession of it.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:10:1.hebrew: ורב יוסף אמר צריכי שומא - קודם קידושין קאמר, כדפי' בקונטרס. ותימה, דלקמן פ"ב (קידושין דף מח.) תניא גבי "התקדשי לי בשטר חוב": וחכמים אומרים, שמין את הנייר, אם יש בו שוה פרוטה — מקודשת; ומשמע: שמין את הנייר אחר קידושין, ואע"ג דמתחלה שומת הנייר לא היתה ידועה. ויש לומר: דללישנא דאמר "בכל דהו כולי עלמא לא פליגי", איירי דאמר לה כל דהו; וללישנא דבכל דהו נמי פליגי, הכי קאמר: ואם רוצה לקדשה בשטר — שמין את הנייר מתחילה, אם יש בו שוה פרוטה מקודשת; כלומר: אם שמוהו תחילה, לאפוקי ממ"ד מקודשת אע"פ שאין בו שוה פרוטה מטעם שטר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:10:1.english: "And Rav Yosef said: They require an appraisal" - [Rav Yosef] means before the betrothal, as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]. And this is difficult, for later in chapter 2 (Kiddushin 48a), it is taught regarding "Be betrothed to me with a promissory note": "And the Sages say: They appraise the paper; if it has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed." And this implies that they appraise the paper after the betrothal, even though initially the appraisal of the paper was not known! And it can be said that according to the version [of the dispute] that says [that if he said] "whatever [it is worth]," everyone agrees [that an appraisal is not required], [the baraita] is dealing with [a case] where he said to her: "[Be betrothed to me with] whatever [it is worth]." But according to the version [which says] that they disagree even [when he says] "whatever [it is worth]," this is what [the baraita] means: And if he wishes to betroth her with the document, they appraise the paper beforehand; "if it has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed" — that is to say, if they appraised it beforehand, to exclude the opinion of the one who says [that she is] betrothed even though it does not have the value of a peruta, on account of [it being a] document.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:1:1.hebrew: שמע מינה בעלי חיים - פי' בקונטרס: אם נדחו — ידחו לעולם; דאיכא למאן דאמר אין דיחוי אלא בשחוטין, אבל בעלי חיים שנדחו — חוזרים ונראים, ולדידיה קרבה הך בהמה כשחזר ולקח חציה. ושמע מינה דיחוי מעיקרא הוי דיחוי — פירוש: כגון זו שמתחילת הקדישה לא נראית ליקרב, דאיכא מאן דפליג דאין דיחוי אלא בנראה ונדחה. ושמע מינה יש דיחוי בדמים — פירוש: יש תורת דיחוי בדבר שאין קדוש אלא לדמיו, כגון זו שמתחילה לא הקדישה אלא לדמיה שתמכר ויקדשו דמי חציה, שהרי ליקרב לחצאין לא היתה ראויה, ואפילו הכי חל עלה תורת דיחוי לדחות מעל המזבח לעולם, ולא אמרינן אין דיחוי אלא בדבר שהוקדש לגופו ליקרב. ואם תאמר: למה לי למימר הני תרתי, שמע מינה יש דיחוי בדמים ודיחוי מעיקרא? והלא אי אפשר לדיחוי מעיקרא שלא יהא דיחוי בדמים! ויש לומר: דאשכחן דיחוי מעיקרא אף על גב שקדוש קדושת הגוף, כדאמר רבי יוחנן פרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מז.): כגון אכל חלב והפריש קרבן ועבד עבודת כוכבים וחזר בו, והואיל ונדחה כשעבד עבודת כוכבים משום דזבח רשעים תועבה — ידחה. ולאו דוקא נקט התם והפריש קרבן תחלה, דהוא הדין עבד עבודת כוכבים ואחר כך הפריש קרבן, דהשתא הוי דיחוי מעיקרא, דהא רבי יוחנן הוא דאית ליה דיחוי מעיקרא הוי דיחוי; אלא משום אידך מילתא דרבי יוחנן דמייתי התם: אכל חלב והפריש קרבן ונשתטה וחזר ונשתפה, דלא מצי למימר דנשתטה תחילה, כיון דשוטה הוא לאו בר הפרשה הוא, נקט נמי הפריש קרבן ועבד עבודת כוכבים. ואשכחן נמי קדושת דמים אף על גב דלא הוי דיחוי מעיקרא, כגון המפריש נקבה לפסחו וילדה זכר, והוי קדושת דמים — דאין פסח בא מנקבה, ולא הוי דיחוי מעיקרא — שהרי הולד ראוי להקריב. ויש ספרים דגרסינן: שמע מינה קדושת דמים מדחה, ומפרש: דוחה תמורתה מליקרב, מדקתני ותמורתה כיוצא בה. ולא נהירא, דהא בכריתות (דף כח.) גבי מטמא מקדש עשיר שהפריש קן לכבשתו והעני — הואיל ונדחה ידחה, גרסינן נמי שמע מינה תלת כמו בשמעתין, והתם על כרחך אין לפרש קדושת דמים מדחה התמורה, דאין תמורה בעופות, אלא על כרחך היינו קדושה ואינה קריבה. ואם תאמר: למה ליה לרבי יוחנן לאשמועינן הני תלת מילי? הא שמעינן לה בפרק מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צח.)! ויש לומר: משום דפלוגתא היא בפרק בתרא דכריתות (שם), דפליגי בה רבי שמעון בן יוחאי ורבנן, מייתי דברי האמוראים. ויש לתמוה: אמאי לא פריך עלה דרבי יוחנן כי היכי דפריך בסוף כריתות (שם) עלה דרבי אושעיא — דאמר: מטמא מקדש עשיר שהפריש קן לכבשתו והעני, הואיל ונדחה ידחה — דפריך עלה מרבי שמעון, מההיא דאמר: המפריש נקבה [לפסחו קודם הפסח תרעה עד שתסתאב ותמכר ויביא בדמיה פסח], ילדה זכר — ירעה עד שיסתאב וימכר [ויביא בדמיו פסח], ורבי שמעון אומר: הוא עצמו יקרב פסח? ועוד, אדפריך עלה מרבי שמעון, לסייעה עלה מדרבנן, דקאמרי ברישא: ירעה עד שיסתאב! ועוד, כיון דפריך מיחידאה, אדפריך מרבי שמעון דברייתא, לפרוך מרבי אליעזר דמתניתין דתמורה, דתנן פרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף יח:) גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה זכר: רבי אליעזר אומר הוא עצמו יקרב עולה? ויש לומר: היינו טעמא דפריך מרבי שמעון, משום דבההיא אפילו רבנן מודו, דעד כאן לא פליגי רבנן עליה אלא בדבר דשייך ביה קדושת דמים, סברי: מיגו דנחתא ביה קדושת דמים — נחתא ביה נמי קדושת הגוף, וקדושת הגוף לא הוי, שהרי אין פסח בא מן הנקבה; אבל גבי קן — אפילו רבנן מודו, שהרי אין קדושת דמים חלה בעופות. ולמילתא דרבי יוחנן דהכא לא מצי לאותובי, משום דהוה כי ההוא דהמפריש נקבה לפסחו, ואי הוה מותיב מרבי שמעון — הוה אמינא לסיועיה מדרבנן; וממילתא דרבי אליעזר נמי לא מצי לאותביה, משום דהוה יחידאה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:1:1.english: Conclude from it that living things [can be deferred] - Rashi explained: If they were deferred, they are deferred permanently; for there is an authority who holds that deferral applies only to slaughtered offerings, but living animals that were deferred become eligible again, and according to him, this animal would be offered once he acquired its other half. "And conclude from it that deferral at the outset is considered deferral" — explanation: such as this case, where from the beginning of its consecration it was not eligible to be offered; for there is an authority who disagrees, holding that deferral applies only when an offering was once eligible and then deferred. "And conclude from it that there is deferral with regard to monetary value" — explanation: the principle of deferral applies even to an item that is consecrated only for its monetary value, such as this animal, which he initially consecrated only for its monetary value, so that it would be sold and the proceeds from its half would become consecrated, as it was not fit to be offered in halves; and even so, the principle of deferral took effect upon it to defer it from the altar permanently, and we do not say that deferral applies only to an item that was consecrated inherently [with bodily sanctity] to be offered. And if you should say: Why do I need to state both of these — "Conclude from it that there is deferral with regard to monetary value" and "deferral at the outset [is deferral]"? For is it not impossible to have deferral at the outset without it also being deferral of monetary value? And one can say: We find deferral at the outset even though [the animal] is consecrated with bodily sanctity, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said in chapter Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 47a): For instance, one who ate forbidden fat, designated a sacrifice, worshipped idols, and then repented — since it was deferred when he worshipped idols, because "the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination" [Proverbs 21:27], it remains deferred. And it was not strictly necessary [for Rabbi Yoḥanan] to state there that he designated the sacrifice first, for the same law would apply if he worshipped idols and afterward designated the sacrifice — in which case it would be deferral at the outset, as it is Rabbi Yoḥanan who maintains that deferral at the outset is considered deferral. Rather, because of that other statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan cited there — one who ate forbidden fat, designated a sacrifice, became mentally incompetent, and then regained competence, where he could not say that he became mentally incompetent first, since an incompetent person is not capable of designation — he likewise formulated [the idolatry case as]: designated a sacrifice and then worshipped idols. And we also find monetary sanctity even though it is not deferral at the outset, such as one who designates a female for his Paschal offering and it gives birth to a male. This is monetary sanctity, because a Paschal offering cannot come from a female; yet it is not deferral at the outset, as the offspring was [inherently] fit to be offered [at birth]. And there are texts in which we read: "Conclude from it that monetary sanctity defers," and it is explained: it defers its substitute from being offered, as [the Baraita] teaches, "and its substitute is like it." But this is not plausible, for in Keritot (28a), regarding a wealthy person who defiled the Temple and designated a nest of birds for his ewe lamb, and then became poor — since it was deferred, it remains deferred — we also read: "Conclude from it three [rulings]," just as in our sugya; and there, one cannot possibly explain that monetary sanctity defers the substitute, because substitution does not apply to birds! Rather, perforce, it means that it is consecrated but cannot be offered. And if you should say: Why did Rabbi Yoḥanan need to teach us these three things? Behold, we already learned them in the chapter Mi Shehayah Tamei (Pesachim 98a)! And one can say: Because it is a dispute in the last chapter of Keritot (ibid.), where Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai and the Rabbis disagree, [the Gemara] cites the words of the Amoraim [to show whose view they adopt]. And one may wonder: Why did [the Gemara here] not raise a challenge against Rabbi Yoḥanan, just as it challenged Rabbi Oshaya at the end of Keritot (ibid.) — who said: "A wealthy person who defiled the Temple and designated a nest of birds for his ewe lamb, and then became poor — since it was deferred, it remains deferred" — where [the Gemara] challenged him from Rabbi Shimon, from that which was taught: "One who designates a female [for his Paschal offering before Passover, it shall graze until it develops a blemish, and be sold, and with its proceeds he shall bring a Paschal offering]; if it gave birth to a male, it shall graze until it develops a blemish, and be sold, [and with its proceeds he shall bring a Paschal offering]; but Rabbi Shimon says: It itself shall be offered as a Paschal offering"? Furthermore, rather than challenging him from Rabbi Shimon, let [the Gemara] support him from the Rabbis, who state in the first clause: "It shall graze until it develops a blemish"! And furthermore, since [the Gemara in Keritot] challenged from an individual opinion, rather than challenging from Rabbi Shimon in a Baraita, let it challenge from Rabbi Eliezer in the Mishnah in Temurah, as we learned in chapter Elu Kodashim (Temurah 18b) regarding one who designates a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth to a male: "Rabbi Eliezer says: It itself shall be offered as a burnt offering"? And one can say: This is the reason [the Gemara in Keritot] challenged from Rabbi Shimon: because in that case [of a bird offering], even the Rabbis agree. For the Rabbis disagree with him only regarding an item to which monetary sanctity applies, for they hold: Since monetary sanctity descended upon it, bodily sanctity also descended upon it; and yet bodily sanctity cannot take effect, because a Paschal offering cannot come from a female. But regarding a nest of birds, even the Rabbis agree, because monetary sanctity does not take effect upon birds. And as for Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement here, [the Gemara] could not challenge him, because it is like that case of one who designates a female for his Paschal offering; and had it challenged him from Rabbi Shimon, one could say [in defense] that he is supported by the Rabbis. And from the statement of Rabbi Eliezer, too, it could not challenge him, because he was an individual opinion.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:4:1.hebrew: חצייך בפרוטה וחצייך בפרוטה - ואם תאמר: אמאי לא יועיל? והא לא אמר לעיל דלא פשטו קידושין בכולה אלא משום דאיכא דעת אחרת, ואינה מתרצה אלא למה ששומעת; אבל אם היינו יודעים שמתרצה בכולה, פשטו קידושין בכולה, והכא גלי דעתה שמתרצה בכולה! וי"ל: דאי הוי מיירי דאמר לה בלשון קידושין — אין ה"נ דהוו פשטו קידושין בכולה; אבל הכא איירי דאמר לה הרי את מאורסת לי, או בחד מהני לישני דלעיל (קידושין דף ו.):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:4:1.english: "Half of you with a peruta and half of you with a peruta" - And if you say: Why should this not be effective? Behold, did [the Gemara] not say above that kiddushin does not spread to all of her only because there is another party's consent [involved], and she only agrees to that which she hears; but if we knew that she agrees to all of her [being betrothed], the kiddushin would spread to all of her, and here she revealed her intention that she agrees to all of her! And one can say: If it were dealing with [a case where] he spoke to her using the language of kiddushin — indeed, the kiddushin would have spread to all of her; but here, it is dealing with [a case where] he said to her: "Behold, you are betrothed to me," or with one of those [other] expressions from above (Kiddushin 6a).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:5:1.english: "Half of you with a peruta today, and half of you with a peruta tomorrow" - He said this to her all at once.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:7:1.hebrew: שתי בנותיך לשני בני - אומר ר"י, דמיירי בבנות קטנות, דקידושין דאב נינהו; דאי בגדולות, ואב מקבל קידושין בתורת שליחות — פשיטא דבעי פרוטה לכל אחת, דשליח לא עדיף ממשלחו. דבתר נותן דקאמר — לאו דוקא, שהרי הנותן ע"כ בתורת שליחות בניו הוא בא; ואי בתר נותן אזלינן — הוי בעי שתי פרוטות, כאילו הבנים בעצמם מקדשין. אבל הבעיא היא אי בתר מקבל אזלינן לגמרי, דשמא אין לחוש אלא שיקבל המקבל שוה פרוטה. וצ"ל שבירר לאיזה מהם, כגון רחל לראובן ולאה לשמעון; דאל"כ — הוי קידושין שלא נמסרו לביאה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:7:1.english: "Your two daughters to my two sons" - The Ri says that [the Gemara] is dealing with minor daughters, for the betrothal belongs to the father; for if [it dealt] with adult daughters and the father receives the betrothal [money] by virtue of agency, it is obvious that a peruta is required for each one, as an agent is no better than his principal. And that which [the Gemara] says, "[Do we follow] the giver," is not exact, for the giver perforce acts by virtue of the agency of his sons, and if we were to follow the giver, two perutot would be required, as if the sons themselves were betrothing. Rather, the dilemma is whether we follow the recipient entirely, as perhaps there is no concern other than that the recipient receives the value of a peruta. And it must be said that he specified which of them [is for which] — such as Rachel to Reuven and Leah to Shimon — for if not so, it would be a betrothal that cannot lead to marital relations.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:8:1.hebrew: בתך ופרתך בפרוטה - כיון דפרה אין נקנית בכסף, שדינא להו בתר בתו. והדר בעי: ״בתך וקרקעך״, דקרקע נקנה בכסף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 7b:8:1.english: "Your daughter and your cow with one peruta" - Since a cow is not acquired with money, we assign [the money] to his daughter. And afterwards, [the Gemara] asks [about] "your daughter and your land," for land is acquired with money.
